- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates prices during prolonged bullish sentiment runs; add a 0.5–1.5% upward bias for 5–7 day horizons.
- Model overestimates during bearish sentiment runs; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for 5–7 day horizons.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–2% at the shift point.
- Model shows persistent lag in price direction; if true price moves >2% from recent mean, adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate in early days of a bullish trend; cap forecast at +1.5% above recent 7-day high.
